subject: Displaying Plots Using the Same Units

messages.author: 0cb1ab1dff2bfeb6
messages.subject: Displaying Plots Using the Same Units
parts:
Hello, I've managed to generate KDE, AKDE, and WAKDE plots for my lizard tracking data. It seems however that some plots are displayed using meters while others are displayed using kilometers. Is there any way I can specify what units I want my plots to be displayed in  so it's consistent for all individuals? Thanks!

Jason

messages.author: 7d868ffe3daa8319
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Displaying Plots Using the Same Units
parts:
Hi Jason,

In your summary() line, you can add units=FALSE as an argument, which will standardize everything to the same units.

Jesse

Thanks so much! The plots are displaying in the same units now, though out of curiosity is there any way to change the default unit from meters to kilometers?  

     One last related question has popped up. I've noticed that when I view my home range area estimates using the summary function that the estimates for different individuals are in different units, with some being in hectares and others being in square kilometers. Is there a similar fix to get these KDE estimates displayed in the same units? I've tried adding units="FALSE" to the akde function, but that doesn't seem to help. Here's an example of my current code, with individuals 1 and 5 having home range estimates in hectares and square kilometers respectively:

#Loop to calculate KDE estimates

KDE<-list()
for(i in 1:length(gila))
{
  print(i)
  M.IID <- ctmm.fit(gila[[i]])
  KDE[[i]] <- akde(gila[[i]],M.IID)
}
names(KDE)<-names(gila)

#Getting home range area estimates for individuals

summary(KDE[[1]])

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Displaying Plots Using the Same Units
parts:
Hi Jason,

You just need to take the quote marks "" off of FALSE. TRUE and FALSE (or T and F) are boolean values in R, whereas quote marks enclose character/string values.

As for getting all plots into kilometers, you could leave the units argument alone and expand the plotting limits to be at least a kilometer across, then the units will automatically switch over. It wouldn't be hard for me to add an option to fix the units, though. I will add that to the to-do list.

Best,
Chris
